title: A prompt template fills in a prompt that is sent often
body:
Every prompt in coax is typed into the input box from scratch. The one way to reuse an old prompt is `/history`, which lists the prompts sent in the session for picking one again. Some prompts Jack sends follow the same shape every time, with only a few parts changing:

- A list of tasks, how long he will be away, and a request for any questions before he goes.
- "Do commits, cleanups, and foam bookkeeping", sent word for word.

## Proposal

A prompt template is a named prompt with blanks to fill in. Choosing one opens it in the input as a short form, one field per blank, and sending it fills the blanks into the template text. A template with no blanks is sent as it stands, so it works as a shortcut for a fixed prompt.

```text
away: tasks (a list), time away
  {tasks}

  I'm stepping out for {time}, so get through as much of this as you can.
  Any questions before I go?
```

## Open

- Where templates are defined: coax's `config.toml`, or a file of their own beside it.
- How a template is chosen: a slash command such as `/away`, a picker like `/history`'s, or a key.
- Whether the form is a set of fields drawn in the input, or the template text placed in the input with its blanks marked for editing in place.
- Whether a list field takes one item per line.
close_reason: Landed in 14c84b0, with the /t box, Tab completion and single-Enter commands from the last note.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Jack chose these answers to the open questions:

- Templates live in `config.toml`, one table per template under `[templates.<name>]`.
- A template is chosen with `/t <name>`, which the command list offers as the name is typed.
- Choosing a template places its text in the input with each `{blank}` marked. The cursor starts on the first blank, and Tab moves to the next. This is an edit in place, not a separate form.

The implementer settles the rest. A template with no blanks is sent at once, as the proposal says. A list blank is ordinary text, so a list is typed one item per line with Alt+Enter.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Prompt templates are built, uncommitted on `dev`:

- `src/template.rs` holds `Template` (`text`, and an optional `description`). `Template::fill` turns `{{` and `}}` into single braces and lists the blank names in the order they first appear. `spots` finds where each blank sits in the prompt's text.
- `config.toml` reads `[templates.<name>]` tables. A missing `text` or an unknown key is an error naming the file.
- `/t` is a built-in coax command. Enter on `/t` fills `/t `, and the command list then shows the templates with their description, or with the text's first line when there is none. As with the other commands, the first Enter fills a template's name and the second chooses it. `/t <name>` with no such template shows "no template <name>".
- Choosing a template replaces the prompt with its text. The template's blanks are drawn underlined in the accent colour, and the cursor sits on the first one. `App::chosen_blank` records the blank the cursor is on. A typed character or a paste replaces that blank, and Backspace or Delete removes it whole. Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and the previous blank, coming round at either end. Any other key leaves the blank as it is.
- Enter while a blank is unfilled sends nothing. It shows "fill in {name} first" and puts the cursor on that blank. A template with no blanks is sent as soon as it is chosen. Ctrl+U and a send forget the template's blanks.

## Open

- An escaped `{{x}}` whose `x` is also one of the template's blanks becomes `{x}` in the prompt and counts as that blank.
- A list blank is ordinary text, typed one item per line with Alt+Enter. Nothing shapes it into a list.
- The README does not mention templates. Its config section is Jack's.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Jack asked for a second way in, and for two changes that reach every command:

- `/t` then Enter opens a list box of every template with its description, like `/history`'s. `j`/`k` or the arrow keys move, Enter chooses and Esc closes.
- Tab completes a command name from the command list. Tab again cycles through the matches in list order, and Shift+Tab goes back. This holds for every `/` and `//` command, template names after `/t ` included.
- Enter on a complete command name runs it at once, where it used to take one Enter to fill in the name and a second to run it. Enter on a prefix that matches exactly one command runs that one. `//` agent commands still open their confirmation box before anything is sent.

The single Enter changes how an existing key behaves, so the next release moves the minor.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Jack asked for a second way into templates and for the command list to take Tab and a single Enter. This landed, uncommitted:

- `/t` and Enter, or `/t ` with nothing after it, open a box listing the templates with their descriptions. The box is `MenuTarget::Templates`, drawn like the `/history` box. Up, Down, `j` and `k` move, Enter chooses, Esc closes. With no templates configured, the prompt's rule says "no templates in config.toml".
- Tab in the command list fills in the first match for what was typed, and further Tabs cycle through the matches in the list's order, with Shift+Tab going back. `App::command_cycle` keeps the typed text, so the cycle runs over its matches rather than the narrower matches of the name just filled in. Any edit ends the cycle. With no list open, Tab still moves between a template's blanks.
- Enter runs a command at once when the prompt names it in full, or when only one command matches. With several matches, Enter does nothing until Up or Down picks one, which `App::command_picked` records, and then Enter runs the picked entry. Before, a first Enter filled in the name and a second ran it. `//` commands still stop at the confirmation box, which a single Enter now reaches.

Tests cover the template box, `/t ` with nothing after it, a complete template name, Tab and Shift+Tab over templates and over commands, several matches waiting, a picked entry, a unique prefix, and `//` with a unique prefix reaching the confirmation. Five older tests were rewritten for the single Enter.
